thread:
maria: Heads-up — console LCP is spiking on heatmap & metric panes after yesterday's telemetry-proxy deploy. EU canary numbers: 4.2s -> 6.8s.

oliver: Saw the same. Canary traces show main-thread parse + eval up, and waterfall shows bundle download + parse longer than usual. Looks like something got inlined.

maria: Repro steps: open Projects > Dashboard > Heatmap, apply 7d range, expand legend. Network: main.bundle.js ~980KB gz, but sources show telemetry-client imported into main instead of chunked.

sam: Quick question — did we change any bundler entries or the telemetry init recently?

ana: We merged a tiny change that eager-initializes telemetry to reduce startup latency: `telemetry-client/init` was added to `src/index.ts` to warm sockets. I thought it was lazy, but maybe tree-shaking failed.

oliver: I toggled the canary env `REACT_APP_TELEMETRY_EAGER=false` locally -> canary LCP dropped from 6.8s to ~4.6s. That points to eager-init being the main culprit.

maria: Interesting — that explains runtime cost, but why +300KB in main bundle? Any polyfills pulled in?

sam: Ran a quick bundle analyze: telemetry-client pulls in `@format/intl` shim and a small `perf-shim` which were previously in an async chunk. Looks like the new import path prevented code-splitting.

jing: And I noticed a routing policy tweak last week: we shifted some traffic to EU cache tier by changing `kv-affinity` weights. Could that affect cache hit patterns and cause extra re-fetch + parse cycles?

sam: Yep — the routing change increased cross-region reads, so even if caching exists, more responses are larger and page has to parse them more often. Combined with bigger main bundle = higher parse time.

ana: Proposed quick remediation:
1) rollback eager telemetry init in canary (IMMEDIATE)
2) change bundler entry so telemetry-client is loaded via `import('./telemetry-client')` (lazy)
3) audit for accidental polyfill imports (`intl`, `perf-shim`) and add explicit sideEffects: false where safe
4) revert the `kv-affinity` weight tweak or tune it to reduce cross-region fetches while we investigate

maria: @deploy-bot can we rollback canary deploy c-2026-04-18? Need to confirm perf improvement before next canary.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollback for canary c-2026-04-18 initiated. ETA ~5m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

oliver: After rollback, canary LCP back to ~4.3s. Confirmed main bundle size reduced ~260KB gz.

sam: I'll open a PR today to lazy-load telemetry and add a jest/perf check asserting main bundle gz < 700KB for CI. Patch will also gate eager init behind `window.__REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_READY`.

jing: I'll file a routing-policy ticket to audit the `kv-affinity` change and measure cross-region fetch delta. Will add a small benchmark to simulate dashboard read patterns.

maria: Thanks all. Follow-ups: PR from @sam, routing ticket from @jing, and an RFC to formalize bundling rules (no direct imports that pull in intl/polyfills into main). Putting these in #eng-platform backlog.

sam: One-liner code suggestion to lazy-load:
```js
// src/index.tsx
if (process.env.REACT_APP_TELEMETRY_EAGER === 'true') import('./telemetry-client').then(m => m.init());
else setTimeout(() => import('./telemetry-client').then(m => m.init()), 2000);
```

maria: That looks good. Let's keep the delayed init for now until we have a vetted lazy-load pattern. :+1:
